You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Demo follow-through for interactive ARC puzzles

Use when an interactive ARC evaluation provides demonstrations at a cost and requires exactly one action per turn.

## Procedure
1. On each new turn, read the latest feedback and current grid as the authoritative puzzle state.
2. After a demo arrives, map input/output differences cell-by-cell. Record preserved markers, changed coordinates, color changes, and any geometry linking the changes.
3. Assess whether this evidence uniquely supports an operation. If uncertainty remains and another demo is affordable, request one; otherwise make the best evidence-supported grid submission rather than inventing tool activity.
4. Keep the response focused on the game protocol: exactly one action JSON as the final line. Do not call unrelated tools or insert placeholder calculations; every non-action step must materially advance rule inference.
5. Validate submitted dimensions, row lengths, and values, and preserve cells not supported by the inferred transformation.

## task-57fd39bf recurrence: unresolved selector, 8 demos / capped failure
Fresh instance test 19x24, bg2, marker7. Test has sparse/structured regions in rows 3-4 and 14-15, others bg. Eight demos showed suffix/tail recoloring to color1 on selected rows, but selection criteria remained unresolved; task ID alone does not select variant.

Demo deltas:
1) 11x22 bg6 marker7: row6 had marker run c0-13 then bg tail c14-21; changed tail to 1. Row10 fully marker c0-21 unchanged. This might look like trailing-suffix fill, but later examples disprove simplistic selector.
2) 24x9 bg9 marker8: row3 full marker unchanged. Row13 markers c0-5 and bg tail c6-8 ->1.
3) 18x14 bg2 marker0: only row16 c13 changed 2->1. Row16 had a long initial run c0-4; there were other varied marked rows. No broad rule established.
4) 29x25 bg9 marker4: only rows2-4 had alternating 1s/9s at right-side columns c17-24 recolored to alternating 1/9? Output exact tail became checker sequence on rows2-4 (row2 c17=1,c18=9,...c24=1; row3 c17=1,c18=9,...c24=1; row4 c16=1,c17=9,...c24=1), while rows15-17 had right-side alternating 4/9 pattern and were unchanged. This suggests another-color/shape interaction, not generic suffix fill.
5) 12x20 bg3 marker6: row0 full 6 unchanged; row4 had c0-18=6,c19=3 and became c19=1. Row9 c0-16=6,c17-19=3 became c17-19=1.
6) 15x10: bg9; row0 full 3 unchanged; row8 begins with three 3s then bg tail c3-9 ->1.
7) 20x8 bg6 marker2: row2 c0-4=2 then tail c5-7 ->1; full marker row12 unchanged.
8) 22x22 bg6 marker8: only row17-18 right tails c19-21 turned 1; other similar sequences remained unchanged. Row17 motif c15-18=8 followed bg c19-21; row18 motif c16-18=8 followed bg c19-21.

Submissions repeatedly attempted to recolor test row15 tail c19-23 to 1 (and sometimes row14 tail c17-23) and were wrong. Several submissions were rejected as invalid ARC grid despite intended 19x24; avoid copy errors and validate all row widths. Final cap reached (8 wrong incl invalids; note evaluator displayed 7 then final 8). No successful test transformation inferred. Keep unresolved; do not reuse a speculative test suffix-fill. New discriminating evidence needed for future recurrence.

## task-57fd39bf additional solved variant
A fresh instance with the same ID was solved correctly after 2 demos. Demo 1 showed selected rows' trailing background suffixes changed to color 1, but selection was unresolved. Demo 2 reinforced this: bg8/marker2, row1 trailing c15, row2 trailing c14-15 changed to 1, while other patterned rows with trailing background remained unchanged. Test bg3/marker5: only row13 had its trailing suffix recolored, c14-18 -> 1; all other cells preserved. Accepted. This supports recoloring the right-edge tail on selected marker-pattern rows, but the row selector is not fully understood; use fresh demos and avoid broad suffix filling. A prior same-ID variant remained unresolved, so do not presume every variant has identical selector.

## task-e77bcc06: singleton diagonal expansion, unresolved transfer

Instance test was 1x17, bg0, seed 2 at c8. Three demos all map a 1xN input with a centered singleton 2 to an NxN output, but test transfer remained unresolved after three demos and eight incorrect submissions. Do not treat any proposed test grid as validated.

Exact demos (0-indexed):
- Demo 1: input 1x13 seed2 c6; output 13x13. Color2 forms widening diagonal arms centered at c6, rows0-6: row0 c6; row1 c5,7; row2 c4,8; row3 c3,9; through row6 c0,12. Rows after 6 contain only 1s in periodic diagonal bands. 1 positions: r3 c5; r4 c6; r5 c3,c7; r6 c4,c8; r7 c1,c5,c9; r8 c2,c6,c10; r9 c3,c7,c11; r10 c0,c4,c8,c12; r11 c1,c5,c9; r12 c2,c6,c10.
- Demo 2: input 1x5 seed2 c2; output 5x5. Color2 V: r0 c2; r1 c1,3; r2 c0,4. Color1 r3c1 and r4c2 only.
- Demo 3: input 1x7 seed2 c3; output 7x7. Color2 V: r0c3; r1 c2,4; r2 c1,5; r3 c0,6. Color1: r3c2; r4c3; r5 c0,c4; r6 c1,c5.

Common evidence: top-down 2 diagonal expansion to edges, with 1s beginning around row3 on diagonals. Color1 extent/periodicity in demo1 differs substantially from shorter demos. Test width17 extrapolation is not established.

Eight wrong test submissions (do not repeat): all used 17x17 outputs with variants of expanding/reflected 2 arms and/or period-four 1 stripe lattices at different phases/extent; every one was rejected. Blanket diagonal 1 stripes with period4 and reflecting the 2 V across full height are disproven. No correct test answer inferred. On future same-ID recurrence, use live demos and avoid phase-only variants of these outputs.

## task-78615fcc fresh-instance lesson: infer period from test clue congruence

A fresh 20x20 test was solved after 8 demos and one wrong submission. Its input clues occupied `r+c` diagonals: 7 at sums 1 and 2; 1 at sum 23; 3 at sums 29, 30, 31; 5 at sums 32,33,34,35. Accepted output tiled the whole plane with period 4: residue map `(r+c) mod 4` is 0→5, 1→3, 2→7, 3→1. The mistaken initial submission extrapolated plausible color runs as a period-14 pattern and was rejected. Key method: enumerate small periods consistent with ALL test clues, assign colors by residue, and select the shortest conflict-free period; don't extrapolate streak lengths. Demonstrations varied substantially (diagonal grids, periodic rows, no-op), so use test clues to select the actual period. Preserve exact modulo phase from top-left (r=0,c=0). Output validated correct.
See `references/task-7c088f59-current-2026-09-29-failure.md` for the full eight-demo delta ledger and all failed test hypotheses from 2026-09-29. Selector remains unresolved; none of the outputs was correct. Do not reuse guesses.

## task-1637756e caution

#### Fresh 11x15 variant, eight demos and eight wrong submissions (2026-09-29)
Test bg9, marker8. Exact marker coordinates (0-based): r1 c1-3,c5,c7-11,c14; r2 c1,c14; r3 c14; r4 c1,c14; r5 c14; r6 c1,c14; r7 c1; r8 c1,c14; r9 c1-14. Eight demos varied greatly; all demonstrated selective bg-to-2 edits in contextual horizontal/vertical/frame-like locations, and often left similar collinear gaps unchanged. Demo1 was an unchanged outline. Remaining examples included selected cells on edges/rails and vertical tracks, never supporting universal interpolation.

Eight test submissions all failed: (1) recolor r1c4,c6,c12,c13 and r9c2; (2) broad interior fill between c7-11 plus c1/c7/c13 vertical intervals and r9c2; (3) r3c14,r5c1; (4) r7c14; (5) unchanged; (6) r3c1; (7) repeated guess 1; (8) repeated guess 4. Instance capped. Exact output selector remains unresolved; these candidates are falsified. For future task-1637756e variants, use only new demo evidence and avoid these hypotheses; identical task IDs have distinct rules.
After 8 demos and 8 failed submissions, the task's common operation is selective collinear marker-gap recoloring to 2, but globally filling every consecutive horizontal/vertical marker gap fails. Some framed patterns have only select interior row gaps filled; many other collinear intervals remain untouched. Map exact changed and unchanged intervals to infer the selector before acting. Machine-validate output, but note some evaluator rejects were reported as invalid despite generated dimensions being checked; reproduce the input exactly and validate JSON/shape.

### Fresh 8-demo unresolved variant (2026-09-29): comprehensive evidence, no test solve
Test: 12x14, background 5, marker 0. Markers: r2 c4-9; r4 c3,c9; r5 c9; r6 c3,c9; r7 c9; r8 c3,c9; r9 c3,c9; r11 c3-7 and c9. Four test submissions failed: (a) fill all row/column intervals; (b) only vertical c3 gaps plus bottom c8; (c) c3/c9 selective gaps and bottom c8; (d) fill rectangular horizontal spans between c3/c9 in rows 4,6,8,9 plus c3 gaps and c8. Further repeated/expanded guesses also failed; final cap after eight wrong submissions. Do not reuse these predicted test outputs or selectors.

Eight demos show edit color 2 but highly selective ray/line behavior. D1 mostly preserved a large scaffold; selected isolated cells on columns 4 and 10 changed. D2 frame-like outline: top row gap c7-8 and one hole on right border at r7,c11 changed; rest untouched. D3 sparse markers on columns 4 and 8: selected ray cells on these columns and top/bottom horizontal spans changed, many aligned gaps left unchanged. D4 repeated row motifs: inserted 2s at selected boundaries of marker runs, plus sparse columns 2 and 17 along certain rows. D5 similar sparse rows/columns: selected between-marker cells on rows 3/20 and selected vertical locations c0/c16. D6 demonstrates a striking pattern: marker at (7,6) casts horizontal 2 ray rightward c7-11 toward marker at c11; selected vertical rays on c6 and c11; other cells unchanged. D7 sparse marker shape: row6 horizontal gaps c2,c4-5,c7-8 filled; vertical rays on c0 and c8 at selected rows. D8 background5 marker8: row0 horizontal rays fill c2-5,c7-8,c10-12; vertical columns c1/c14 have selected gaps at specific rows; many cells remain unchanged.

Broad horizontal/vertical interpolation is disproven. The unresolved selector likely involves directed rays/projections from selected marker endpoints and a structural/line pattern, but evidence does not yield reliable transfer. Future recurrence: map each demo's exact deltas, distinguish ray direction and anchor motif, identify unchanged candidate rays, and request discriminating demos before spending submissions. Never infer test output from task ID or simply close its apparent rectangle. This instance ended at attempt cap with no accepted output.


## Pitfalls
- A demo response is the moment to use the evidence immediately; do not defer analysis behind irrelevant tool calls.
- Do not infer a transform from colors or sparse motifs alone; establish it from actual changed cells.
- Never claim a result of a computation that was not performed. For trivial coordinate mapping, reason directly; for nontrivial transforms, use a calculation tool only when permitted by the interaction.
- Respect the required action format even when more analysis is useful: each turn must end in exactly one action JSON.

# Partitioned grid summary inference

## When to Use
Use when full-length separator lines divide an ARC grid into panels/compartments and the output is a smaller grid or a summary of aligned regions.

Use when long straight lines divide ARC inputs into repeated compartments and output is smaller than input.

## Workflow
1. Map full separator rows/columns and distinguish intermittent values from separator. Enumerate compartments/paired panels and infer dimensions from demos.
2. Align every output cell with candidate source unit; test counts, presence, equality, parity, corners, majority, and other predicates against complete demos.
3. A plausible visual correspondence is not enough; verify positive and negative positions across multiple examples.
4. Construct output only after the rule is confirmed. Validate shape, widths, and values. When ambiguous and affordable, request another demonstration rather than guessing.
5. Similar task IDs can recur with different selectors. Treat prior solutions as hypotheses, not proof.

## task-fe9077c7 paired-field equality mask: validated recurrence

A full uniform separator row/column can split equal-sized noisy panels. In this supported recurrence, retain the upper/left panel (exclude separator and other panel), preserving its background B. At each aligned coordinate, output 3 iff the two original panel cells are exactly equal; otherwise output B. This is positionwise equality, not a direct transfer of either panel's exception mask. Orientation may be horizontal or vertical. Verify current demos because the same task ID has contradictory recurrences.

Additional confirmed vertical-split instance: demo input 28x5 with full-height separator column c2=7. Left/right panels are 28x2. Output is 28x2, with 3 where aligned cells are exactly equal and 5 otherwise (the left-panel background). Examples: row0 `(5,5)` and `(5,2)` gives `[3,5]`; row3 `(5,2)` and `(5,5)` gives `[5,3]`. Solved test input 5x19 had separator c9=2, two 5x9 panels, base 0. Accepted output:
`[[0,0,0,0,0,3,0,0,0],[0,0,0,0,3,0,3,3,0],[0,0,0,0,0,0,3,0,3],[0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,3],[0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0]]`.
This directly confirms the rule for vertical panels with unequal backgrounds/noisy values.

Latest fresh instance solved correctly after one wrong submission and five demos. Test input 27x17, separator row13 all 4. Retained upper 13x17: background 5, noise 0. Lower 13x17: background 2, noise 5. Correct output: 3 exactly at aligned positions where upper and lower values are equal (in this test upper=5 and lower=5); otherwise 5. Accepted output had 38 threes. Exact 0-indexed equality coordinates:
(0,14), (1,5),(1,12), (2,2),(2,4),(2,9), (3,2),(3,14), (4,6),(4,10), (5,3),(5,11),(5,14), (6,11),(6,14), (7,4),(7,7),(7,11),(7,13), (8,2),(8,3),(8,10), (9,2),(9,5),(9,14), (10,0),(10,3),(10,6), (11,0),(11,5),(11,7),(11,9),(11,12),(11,14), (12,1),(12,2),(12,8),(12,14). All other output values are 5. Submission marked CORRECT.

Current-instance demos:
- D2 (11x9; separator row5; output 5x9, base 8): sole output3 at (3,3); aligned top and bottom are both 8 (top row3 c3=8, lower row9 c3=8). Correct bottom alignment is separator+1+r.
- D3 (19x10; separator row9; output top 9x10, base 6): output3 at (0,6),(1,3),(2,5),(2,7),(5,5),(6,6),(8,1),(8,4); these align equal 6s.
- D4 (19x14; separator row9; output top 9x14, base 0): output3 at (0,11),(0,12),(1,1),(1,2),(1,9),(1,10),(3,3),(3,8),(3,12),(4,2),(6,9),(6,13),(7,7),(8,2),(8,3),(8,12); these are aligned equal 0s.
- D5 (21x9; separator row10; output upper 10x9, base 9): output3 at (0,2),(1,8),(2,7),(4,0),(4,2),(5,1),(6,7),(7,8),(8,6); exactly aligned equal 9s.
- D1 vertical separator col12, output left panel 11x12 with base 5. Align right panel starting input col13; compare equal cells at same row and relative column.

There is also a distinct solved recurrence with 13x5 input split at row6: upper 6x5 background 4/exceptions 2, lower 6x5 background 4/exceptions 7; output equality mask:
[[4,4,4,4,4],[3,4,4,3,3],[4,3,4,4,3],[4,4,4,4,4],[3,3,4,4,3],[4,4,3,4,4]]. Equality coordinates (1,0),(1,3),(1,4),(2,1),(2,4),(4,0),(4,1),(4,4),(5,2).

Caution: a historical same-ID instance was unresolved after 8 demos and 8 wrong attempts; simple equality was not established there. Thus apply equality only when live demos support it. In vertical splits, output relative col c maps to input left c and right separator+1+c. In horizontal splits, output row r maps to input top r and bottom separator+1+r. Validate dimensions and row widths.

## task-428024d7 verified recurrence: 3x3 block mode, ignore separator/background color

The input is tiled into 3x3 blocks; output has one cell per block, in row-major order. For each block, output the most frequent color **other than the uniform background/separator color** (5 in solved instances). Crucial: color 0 is an ordinary candidate when background is 5, and can win; do not discard zero by assuming it is background. Demonstrations across 21x21→7x7, 18x18→6x6, 27x27→9x9, 24x24→8x8, 9x9→3x3, and 30x30→10x10 support blockwise mode excluding 5. A wrong test submission in one instance used the most frequent nonzero/non-5 value, incorrectly writing 5 in many output cells; corrected method includes zero among candidates and was accepted. Another fresh 30x30 instance was directly solved with the same rule: output 10x10 and only colors 0/8 after excluding 5. Code pattern: for each 3x3 block tally cells !=5; choose mode, or 0 if all cells are 5. Tie behavior remains unestablished; check demos if ties occur. This recurrence is particularly well-grounded across fresh instances, but confirm the 3x3 tiling and background from the current test/demos.

Implementation: determine background value B from the uniform separator/field. For each output (i,j), tally all 9 cells in input rows `3i..3i+2`, cols `3j..3j+2`, excluding only B; select the mode. If the block is entirely B, output 0 (as supported by examples). Validate output dimensions H/3 × W/3 and tie behavior when needed.

## task-8841b816 validated recurrence: period-copy sparse motifs across panel grid

A separator row and repeated separator columns define rectangular panels; the transformation propagates the sparse marker pattern from the initial panel across the panel array, without changing separators/background. Current demos establish both propagation axes and output period.

Demo 1 (8x26): vertical separator columns c=8 and c=17 (color 4), panels of width 8; there is no horizontal separator. The 8-row motif in leftmost panel (columns 0–7) is copied identically into the middle and right panels (offsets +9 and +18, respecting separator columns). Every marker is literal: e.g. row1 [1,8,5] at c0,c2 copied to c9,c11,c18,c20; row6 marker 7 at c7 copied c16,c25. Existing values in subsequent panels do not override motif (they were background in this demo).

Demo 2 (8x9): full vertical separator c=4, color5; one panel on each side, each width 4. The sparse markers in left panel columns 0–3 are copied to right panel with +5 offset, preserving the separator and originals. Evidence: row0 color6 at c1 -> c6; row3 color4 c2 -> c7; row5 color4 c0 -> c5; row6 color1 c0 -> c5. Other cells remain background 9; separator unchanged.

Demo 3 (15x20): vertical separators c=6,c=13 (color3), and full horizontal separator row7 (color3). Panels are 7 columns wide and top/bottom sections are 7 rows high. The initial top-left 7x6 interior motif (columns0–5, rows0–6) is tiled horizontally into other panels and copied vertically into bottom section, with offsets +7 rows / +7 columns per panel (including separator positions: panel starts at c0,c7,c14; separators occupy c6,c13). Preserve separator lines and background. Examples: r0 marker4 at c18 propagates to c4,c11,c18; r1 marker9 c16 propagates c2,c9,c16; r6 marker8 c14 propagates c0,c7,c14. Entire 7x20 top pattern repeats identically in rows8–14. Input marker in each demo's later panels may provide corroborating evidence, but output fills all corresponding locations.

Test grid (9x11): vertical separators c=3 and c=7, color1; horizontal separator row4, color1. Repeated panel geometry: 3-column interiors per panel (cols0–2,4–6,8–10), 4-row halves (rows0–3 and 5–8). The top-left 4x3 seed motif is copied to each of the other two panels and repeated in the lower section. Correct solved output:
[[9,6,6,1,9,6,6,1,9,6,6],
 [6,6,9,1,6,6,9,1,6,6,9],
 [3,6,6,1,3,6,6,1,3,6,6],

# ARC demo grounding

Use with an ARC-solving skill when a puzzle offers costly demonstrations and submissions.

## task-55b70234 recurrence: fill framed interiors and 3x3 centers (expanded validation)

This task family uses shape-specific interior recoloring. Do not apply one fill color indiscriminately to every hollow outline: identify frame geometry and the corresponding center/interior color from demos.

A prior solved instance (background 8) demonstrated hollow 5x5 frames with 3x3 interiors filled 7, and a separate 3x3 block with its center changed to 7. Another test was solved correctly by filling the 5x5 frame's 3x3 cavity 7 and replacing the missing center of a separate 3x3 color9 object with 7.

Expanded recurrence, additional current validated variant (one demo; test solved on third submission with two wrong attempts): background 3. Demo shows a 7x7 outline with interior 5x5 filled 7; a separate 3x3 outline with only center empty has its center changed to 7. Test contained (a) 4x4 outline color4 with 2x2 cavity -> fill 2; (b) 7x7 outline color1 with 5x5 cavity -> fill 7; (c) 3x3 color8 object missing center -> center becomes 7. These reinforce the cavity-size mapping: 2x2 ->2, 3x3/5x5 ->7, and isolated center hole in 3x3 ->7. Validate grid serialization strictly: prior first guess malformed due wrong row width; second structurally valid but wrong because it used 7 for 2x2 cavity. Correct output preserves all outlines/exterior and applies the corresponding interior fill.

Expanded recurrence, 3 demos, test solved after five wrong submissions:
- Demo 1: 10x10 bg4; 7x7 square frame of 6 at rows1–7, cols0–6, cavity rows2–6, cols1–5 -> 7. This is a 5x5 interior. Confirms the large framed cavity fill color 7.
- Demo 2: 30x18 bg8. Multiple objects: 7x7 frame of 9 at r2–8,c4–10, interior 5x5 ->7; 3x3 frame of 3 at r1–3,c13–15 with one missing center at r2,c14 ->7; 4x4 frame of 3 at r10–13,c11–14 with 2x2 interior r11–12,c12–13 ->2; 9x7 frame of 6 at r14–20,c2–8 with interior r15–19,c3–7 ->7; 3x3 frame of 1 at r16–18,c10–12 with missing center ->7; another 3x3 frame of 1 at r21–23,c10–12 center ->7; 3x3 frame of 9 at r26–28,c5–7 center ->7; 3x3 frame of 0 at r26–28,c10–12 center ->7. Note the 2x2 cavity specifically filled with 2; multiple frame/component types coexist.
- Demo 3: 15x22 bg8. 5x5 frame of 4 at r0–4,c0–4 interior 3x3 ->7; 4x4 frame of 3 at r1–4,c15–18, interior 2x2 ->2; 5x5 frame of 6 at r6–12,c5–9, interior 5x3 ->7; 6x6 frame of 9 at r7–12,c15–20, interior 4x4 ->2. Thus 3x3 or 5x3 cavities get 7; 2x2 and 4x4 cavities get 2, regardless of frame color. The 3x3 objects with only center empty are also filled 7.

Solved test input 15x20, background 3: a 5x5 frame of 5 at r3–7,c2–6 with 3x3 interior r4–6,c3–5 filled 7; a 3x3 object of 6 at r10–12,c3–5 with center (11,4) changed to 7; a 5x5 frame of 5 at r9–13,c10–14 with 3x3 interior r10–12,c11–13 filled 7; a 7x7 frame of 4 at r0–7,c8–15 with 5x5 interior r1–6,c9–14 filled 2. This last large cavity requires 2, not 7. Correct submission was reached on wrong attempt 6, after five failed guesses.

General inference strongly supported: cavity dimensions determine fill color, at least in observed shapes: 2x2 or 4x4 ->2; 3x3, 5x3, 5x5 ->7. A centered single-cell hole in a 3x3 object ->7. Preserve border and exterior. For future variants, request demos when cavity-size mapping uncertain; don't use one global color for all interiors. Verify exact frame bounds and cavity dimensions.
## task-55b70234: framed cavity fill colors (new demo evidence)

A fresh 11x21 test was solved after the first grid submission was structurally invalid, one demo, and a corrected submission. Demo (11x10, bg=0) shows three separate outlined objects:
- 4x4 color-3 frame at rows0-3, cols0-3; its 2x2 interior (r1-2,c1-2) is filled with 2.
- 4x4 color-6 frame at rows2-5, cols5-8; its 2x2 interior (r3-4,c6-7) is filled with 2.
- 3x3 color-1 frame at rows7-9, cols3-5; its 1x1 center (r8,c4) is filled with 7.
Thus for this instance, 2x2 square cavities receive 2; a single-cell center cavity in a 3x3 outline receives 7. Preserve frames and background/exterior.

Correct test transformation: preserve all four outlines. Fill the 2x2 interior of the 4x4 color-1 frame (rows1-2, cols9-10) with 2. Fill the 3x3 cavity of the 5x5 color-5 frame (rows5-7, cols15-17) with 7. Fill the 3x3 cavity of the 5x5 color-8 frame (rows6-8, cols6-8) with 7. The previously submitted first attempt was INVALID ARC GRID because one row had the wrong width, despite the intended fills; corrected output was accepted. Always machine-check every row length and total dimensions before submission.

## task-d795d9b6 recurrence: marker interval variant with explicit singleton negative evidence
A fresh variant had background 7 and marker 4. In its only demo, row 4 contained markers at columns 2, 3, and 9; output recolored columns 4–8 to 3, leaving the markers intact. This supports recoloring background cells strictly between consecutive markers on a row (there were no demonstrated vertical pairs). The test had background 2 and a single marker 4 at row 1, column 9; correct output is unchanged, since there is no consecutive marker pair. This was accepted. Do not assume singleton markers or simply uniform-looking lines should change. As with other task-d795d9b6 variants, ground from current demos; other recurrences have demonstrated additional row-and-column interval behavior or different rules.

### Newly validated variant (one demo): consecutive-marker interpolation on both axes
A fresh task-d795d9b6 instance had one demo with background 4 and marker 2; the output color was 3. Input-output deltas establish that, on each row and independently on each column, recolor only background cells strictly between consecutive marker cells to 3. Preserve all marker cells and all cells not inside such intervals; use marker positions from the original input. Demo checks: row 0 markers at c3, c6, c9, c13, c17 caused intervening background runs to become 3, while cells outside the first/last bracket stayed 4. Column 3 markers at r9 and r12 caused the intervening r10–11 cells to become 3. Other unbracketed cells remained unchanged. This rule correctly solved the test (bg7, marker5) with horizontal and vertical intervals processed from original marker coordinates. Confirm current demos because this task ID has other variants.

### Solved variant: row/column interpolation independently
чA fresh instance (bg=2, marker=6) had a single demo (bg=1, marker=4; output color=3). The demonstrated rule is to recolor to 3 only background cells strictly between consecutive marker cells in each row and independently in each column. Keep markers unchanged and leave unbracketed cells untouched; use marker coordinates from the original input rather than treating newly filled cells as markers. This explained demo horizontal segments and adjacent markers (no background between them), plus vertical interpolation. Correct test output included horizontal intervals in rows with multiple markers and vertical intervals in columns with multiple markers (e.g. same-column markers at r4/r8 filled r5-r7); accepted with no wrong submissions. This task ID has other variants, so confirm using current demos.

## task-d795d9b6 recurrence: between-marker intervals, demo-validated.

Eight demos established a variant where a uniform-background sparse-marker field is transformed by coloring only the background cells strictly between consecutive markers on each row or column. In the solved instance, bg=1, marker=2, output=3; preserve all markers and all unbracketed cells. Demos 5 and 8 directly show both horizontal and vertical intervals; e.g. demo5 row9 markers at c2 and c25 color c3–24, and demo8 c0 markers at r0 and r4 color r1–3. Snapshot marker locations from the input and process consecutive pairs only. Task ID d795d9b6 has other variants (including rays), so verify current demos.

### Additional solved recurrence variant (3 demos; test accepted)
A fresh task-d795d9b6 instance had sparse marker grids and three highly varied demos, showing the task ID alone does not identify the operation. Backgrounds/markers varied (demo1 bg=0, marker=5; demo2 bg=5, marker=0; demo3 bg=2, marker=6); in all cases output color was 3. Accepted test rule: on each row, recolor the background cells strictly between each pair of *consecutive* marker cells to 3; separately do the same on each column. Keep markers unchanged and preserve all cells not inside these intervals. Use original marker positions (do not let newly colored 3s become endpoints). Demo3 confirmed the rule even for adjacent markers: input row `[6,2,6,2,...]` became `[6,3,6,2,...]`, meaning the background cell between the first two markers became 3, while adjacent marker cells remain untouched. This rule correctly solved the test with bg=7, marker=8, output=3. Earlier incorrect first submission extended intervals across all marker endpoints/lines, coloring unsupported regions; correct approach is consecutive marker pairs only. For implementation: snapshot input; for each row, sort marker columns and fill open intervals between neighbors; then each column, sort marker rows and fill open intervals. Preserve endpoints and unrelated cells. This instance's test had 21x8; accepted output is derivable by that algorithm.

#### Demo2 caution / variant behavior
The second demo had larger bg=5/marker=0 grid and demonstrated substantial changed areas, apparently the same row/column intervals between neighboring markers. Analyze by *consecutive* marker pairs rather than treating every marker line or all spaces as fill. Some cells may appear as changed beyond a visually simple interpolation at first glance; map exact coordinates if another recurrence tests a similar version.

#### Critical lesson from recurrence
A previous skill note claimed eight demos were available; current actual instance proved a similar interpolation mechanism but at three demos, with a strongly atypical third demonstration of two adjacent markers. Do not require minimum marker counts; a pair is enough. D795d9b6 family can feature multiple variants, including rays or other patterns, and historical ID-linked notes are only hypotheses. Ground each new instance in its current demos and any selector evidence; request more if the task’s behavior is not explained by every observed pair.


## task-3f9edb0d: embedded-shape noise cleanup (validated)
One demo: grid background 6, with a uniform 4x4 block of 1s at rows2-5, cols4-7 and a uniform 7x7 block of 2s at rows2-6, cols12-18. Sparse anomalies (including other colors and background-color cells) within these rectangles were all normalized to the block's dominant fill (1 or 2); same-color flecks outside the two rectangles were removed/replaced by background 6. Thus the task extracts solid monochrome rectangles, suppresses scattered noise, and restores outside to background. Current test had background 8, 6x5 block color7 at r0-4,c4-9; 3x3 block color7 at r9-15,c10-12; 5x3 block color4 at r25-27,c8-12. All other non-8 speckles outside those blocks were converted to background 8; cells inside blocks normalized to their solid block colors. The output was accepted. Infer regions from coherent rectangular mass, but verify shapes and any adjacent noise from the current input/demo; dimensions need not match demo.

## Workflow
1. Treat every instance as fresh evidence. Prior task-family patterns can suggest hypotheses, but cannot establish the current rule.
2. Compare demo inputs and outputs cell-by-cell. Record changed coordinates, input/output values, and connected changed regions.
3. Identify candidate sources and targets only after mapping changes. Verify a transformation against multiple regions and demos.
4. Before applying the rule, state which observed changes it explains and which cells remain untouched.
5. If examples show a different geometry or operation from the expected pattern, discard that expectation. Request another demo when uncertainty remains and its cost beats speculation.

## task-d871171c: full-line recoloring to 2 (demo-validated)
A fresh instance demo established: recolor to 2 every complete line whose input cells are all the foreground marker color, preserving all other cells. Demo input 7x10 used background 5 and marker 8. Full vertical columns 3 and 6 (all 8s) were changed to 2, as was full horizontal row 3; partial lines/other cells remained unchanged. In the test, background 4, marker 3: the full bottom row of 3s and full columns 6 and 15 of 3s were recolored 2; partial rows/columns and all remaining cells were preserved. Important serialization pitfall: one submitted grid had row 0 width 21 instead of 22 and was rejected as invalid ARC grid; ensure each row length matches. The corrected exact 5x22 grid was accepted. Current demos establish eligible color by which lines are fully uniform, not assuming a fixed marker color. Check each row/column against original grid and recolor only complete uniform lines.

## Pitfalls
- Familiar colors or sparse markers do not imply a familiar operation; colors can play unrelated roles.
- Do not stop after one plausible local example. Check all changed regions and demos for alignment, preservation, and exceptions.
- Unchanged cells are not evidence of a transformed footprint; base analysis on actual input/output differences.

## Reference
See `references/demo-grounding-example.md` for why changed-cell mapping should precede pattern assumptions.

# Continual-ARC grid submission validation

Use alongside `interactive-arc-evaluation` when an action requires a grid, especially after any evaluator rejection or when grids are generated/edited programmatically.

## Procedure
1. Preserve the input as the baseline. Apply transformations using explicit 0-based coordinates or a repeatable construction, not manual edits to long row strings.
2. Validate the grid dimensions independently: row count equals intended height; every row has exactly intended width; every cell is an integer in 0–9.
3. Validate correspondence to the task: compare untouched areas against the displayed input, check object placement and bounds, and ensure intended edits landed at expected coordinates.
4. Serialize the **entire action object** compactly with a JSON serializer. Parse that exact serialized string back and repeat shape/value checks on the parsed `grid`. Copy the serialized payload verbatim to the final response; do not retype it.
5. If evaluator feedback repeatedly says “not a valid ARC grid” despite local shape checks, do not repeat the same candidate. Re-check coordinate origin, dimensions, unchanged cells, and whether the output should preserve or transform existing objects. These checks reduce serialization risk but do not establish the inferred ARC rule; if rejected, revisit both protocol and rule assumptions.

## Evidence discipline
A structurally valid grid may still be semantically wrong. Treat “invalid grid” feedback as reason to verify payload integrity, but do not assume a serializer/transport fault when outputs all came from one unconfirmed transformation. Separate: (a) JSON shape, (b) ARC grid dimensions and values, (c) demo-supported transformation.

## Related guidance
